blocks.title: VK-PAISNW
blocks.preview: Congratulations! Your loan of Rs 2,00,000 is pre-approved...

blocks.text: Today
Congratulations! Your loan of Rs 2,00,000 is PRE-APPROVED at 0.9% interest. No documents, no salary slip, no CIBIL check required.
Amount will be credited within 30 minutes of paying the one-time file processing charge of Rs 1,850. Ref: PN/AP/77214
Apply here before 6 PM today: paisanow-approval.instant-credit.example.in/apply

actionOptions.label: Open the link to check the offer

reasonOptions.label: A real lender never asks for money before giving a loan
No documents and no credit check is not how lending works
A same-day deadline is used to rush me
The interest rate is good, so it is worth applying

warningSigns: A fee is demanded before any money is given
No documents, salary proof or credit check - real lenders always check
An interest rate far below anything a real lender offers
A same-day deadline removes your time to think
evaluation.feedback: This is an instant-loan fraud. The fee is the fraud - once it is paid the sender disappears and no loan arrives. A genuine lender deducts charges from the loan, never asks you to pay first.

blocks.text: Yesterday
LUCKY DRAW RESULT: Your mobile number has won Rs 15,00,000 in the Bharat Festive Draw 2026. Winner code: BFD-2026-40871.
Today
Second and final reminder. Your claim expires in 48 hours. Send your name, address, Aadhaar number and bank account to release the amount.
Government processing tax of Rs 4,999 is payable before transfer. Reply CLAIM to proceed.

actionOptions.label: Reply CLAIM to find out more
Send the Aadhaar and bank details

reasonOptions.label: I never entered any draw
A real prize never requires a payment from the winner
It asks for Aadhaar and bank details over SMS
It has a winner code, so it looks official

warningSigns: A prize for a draw you never entered
A 'processing tax' must be paid before the money arrives
Aadhaar and bank details are requested over SMS
The message comes from an ordinary mobile number, not a registered sender ID
evaluation.feedback: This is a lottery fraud. No genuine prize requires the winner to pay tax or a fee in advance, and no legitimate body collects Aadhaar or bank details by text message. Notice it came from a personal number, not a company sender ID.

title: Review this text message
instruction: A message about your bank account has arrived.

blocks.title: BZ-KYCVRF
blocks.preview: Dear Customer, your account will be suspended today...

blocks.text: Dear Customer, your Meru Bank account will be SUSPENDED today as your KYC is incomplete. Service request SR-9920174.
Complete verification now to avoid restriction on your account and debit card: meru-kyc-update.secure-verify.example.in

actions.label: Enter card and PIN to verify

actionOptions.label: Call the bank on the number printed on your card
Check KYC status inside the bank's own app
Enter card number and PIN on the page

reasonOptions.label: The web address is not the bank's own address
It threatens to suspend the account the same day
A bank never completes KYC through an SMS link
It quotes a service request number, so it is genuine

warningSigns: The web address is not the bank's real domain
Same-day suspension is threatened to stop you checking
A reference number is quoted to look official - anyone can invent one
Real KYC is never completed through a link in a text message
evaluation.feedback: This is a KYC-freeze fraud. The threat of same-day suspension is there to make you act before thinking. Compare the sender ID with the genuine bank alert already in your inbox, and always use the number printed on your own card.
evaluation.authorNotes: DEVELOPMENT SAMPLE - internally authored, aligned with the approved SMS fraud categories. Replace with client content when received.

blocks.text: Today
TRAFFIC NOTICE: E-challan of Rs 1,000 issued against vehicle no. CH01AK4482 for signal violation on 29/08/2026. Challan no. EC/CH/2026/551203.
Pay within 24 hours to avoid court summons and licence suspension: echallan-payment.trafficdesk.example.in/pay

actionOptions.label: Check on the official transport portal you already use
Check whether the vehicle number is even yours
Pay the 1,000 challan through the link

reasonOptions.label: The link is not the official transport portal
A 24-hour court and licence threat is used to rush me
The vehicle number should be checked before paying anything
It has a challan number and a date, so it must be real

warningSigns: The payment link is not the official transport portal
Court summons and licence suspension within 24 hours is not how challans work
Specific-looking challan and vehicle numbers create false credibility
Real challans can always be checked independently on the official portal
evaluation.feedback: This is an e-challan fraud. Precise-looking numbers and an official tone are easy to fake. A real challan can always be looked up on the official portal yourself - never pay through a link that arrived by SMS.

blocks.preview: Your parcel is on hold at the sorting facility

blocks.text: SwiftPost: Your parcel SP884120375IN is on hold at the sorting facility because the delivery address is incomplete.
Update your address and pay the redelivery handling fee of Rs 58 within 12 hours or the parcel will be returned to sender.
swiftpost-redelivery.parcel-update.example.net/track

actionOptions.label: Check the order in the shopping or courier app itself

reasonOptions.label: The small amount is there to make me pay without thinking
A courier company does not text from a personal mobile number
The tracking number does not match any order I placed
It is only 58 rupees, so there is little risk

warningSigns: The message comes from a personal mobile number, not a company sender ID
A very small fee is used so the amount does not feel worth checking
A 12-hour deadline is attached to a routine delivery
The link is not the courier's real website
evaluation.feedback: This is a parcel fraud. The tiny fee is deliberate - it is small enough that people pay without checking, and the real goal is your card details on the payment page. Always check a delivery inside the app you ordered from.

blocks.text: Today
Hello, I am Neha from CareerBridge HR. Your profile has been shortlisted for a part-time work-from-home data entry role.
Daily payout Rs 2,200 - Rs 2,800 for 2 hours work. No experience or interview needed. Immediate joining.
A refundable registration and ID card charge of Rs 1,200 confirms your seat. Only 4 seats left for this batch.

actionOptions.label: Look up the company independently before replying

reasonOptions.label: A real employer never charges you to start work
No interview and no experience needed is not a real hiring process
The pay is far too high for two hours of data entry
My profile was shortlisted, so it is genuine

warningSigns: A registration fee is demanded before any work begins
The daily pay is far above the market rate for the work described
No interview, no experience and immediate joining
'Only 4 seats left' is pressure, not a fact you can verify
evaluation.feedback: This is a job fraud. Genuine employers pay you, never the other way round, and no real role skips the interview entirely. The 'refundable' fee is never refunded.
evaluation.authorNotes: DEVELOPMENT SAMPLE - internally authored, aligned with the approved SMS fraud categories. Replace with client content when received.

title: Review this text message
instruction: An alert about a debit has arrived.

blocks.text: ALERT: Rs 49,999.00 has been debited from your account for an online purchase at 22:39 today. Txn ID 8841207755.
If this transaction was NOT done by you, call our fraud helpline immediately on 91 74110 39628 to reverse it within 30 minutes.

actionOptions.label: Check the balance in the bank's own app
Call the number printed on your own bank card
Call the helpline number in the message

reasonOptions.label: The 'helpline' is the same number that sent the message
A bank alert does not come from a personal mobile number
A 30-minute reversal window is designed to cause panic
The amount is large, so I should call at once

warningSigns: The 'fraud helpline' is the same mobile number that sent the message
A genuine bank alert comes from a registered sender ID, not a personal number
A 30-minute window is designed to cause panic and stop you checking
The real bank alert already in your inbox looks completely different
evaluation.feedback: This is a callback fraud. There is no debit - the alarm exists only to make you ring the fraudster, who will then walk you into sharing an OTP or installing a screen-sharing app. Check your balance in the bank's own app and call only the number on your card.
evaluation.authorNotes: DEVELOPMENT SAMPLE - internally authored, aligned with the approved SMS fraud categories. Replace with client content when received.

blocks.text: Today
Rs 1,240.00 debited from a/c XX4471 on 02-09-26 at MERU MART. Avl bal Rs 18,362.15. Not you? Call 1800-XXX-4400. -Meru Bank

actionOptions.label: Read it and do nothing - the purchase was mine
Check the balance in the bank app to confirm

reasonOptions.label: There is no link and nothing is asked of me
The account number is masked and the balance is shown
It comes from the bank's registered sender ID
It creates urgency

evaluation.feedback: This is a genuine bank alert. It informs you of a transaction you made, masks the account number, shows the balance, contains no link, and asks for nothing. The helpline it gives is the bank's published number, not a mobile number.

blocks.title: AD-STNHLC
blocks.preview: Reminder: appointment on 05 Sep at 10:30 AM

blocks.text: Today
Reminder: Your appointment at Station Health Centre is on 05 Sep 2026 at 10:30 AM, OPD counter 3. Please carry your ID card.
To reschedule, visit the reception or call the centre during working hours. Do not reply to this message.

actionOptions.label: Note the appointment and carry the ID card
Call the health centre if the time does not suit

reasonOptions.label: It only gives information and asks for nothing
There is no link and no payment request
It asks for money
The sender is an unknown mobile number

evaluation.feedback: This is a genuine appointment reminder. It confirms something you arranged, gives practical details, contains no link, asks for no payment and tells you to use the reception to change it. Ordinary messages like this should not be treated as fraud.

blocks.text: Today
Your electricity bill for Aug 2026 has been generated. Consumer no. 41120887. Amount Rs 1,865.00. Due date 12 Sep 2026.
Pay through the official app or at any collection centre. This message is for information only.

actionOptions.label: Pay through the official app before the due date
Check the consumer number against a previous bill

reasonOptions.label: There is no payment link - it points to the official app
The consumer number matches my own account
It threatens immediate disconnection
It asks for card details

evaluation.feedback: This is a genuine bill notification. It states the amount and due date, quotes your own consumer number, contains no payment link, and directs you to the official app. A fraudulent version would add a link and a same-day disconnection threat.
